sections.overview: Euleia heraclei is a picture-winged fly in the family Tephritidae, found across Europe and Asia Minor.
sections.identification: Adults are about 5 mm long, with broad brown-banded wings; the French park account also notes blue-green eyes.
sections.habitat: Records and crop-host accounts associate it with Apiaceae across Europe and Asia Minor, rather than a single habitat type.
sections.diet: Its larvae mine leaves of celery, celeriac, parsnip, parsley, lovage and related Apiaceae.
sections.behavior: The larvae feed inside leaves, producing blotchy mines; adults occur during the growing season, with timing varying by region.
sections.reproduction: INRAE describes two generations per year: spring adults lay eggs on leaves, and a later generation follows in summer.
sections.ecology: Leaf mining can reduce usable foliage on cultivated hosts, and the fly also develops on wild Apiaceae such as hogweed.
sections.conservation: The consulted accounts treat it as a widespread agricultural pest, not as a species with a conservation assessment.
